The meaning here, the specific things God requires, is not disputed."},{"verse":9,"phrase":"sanctuary","lemma":"ναός","kind":"departure","traditional":"temple","note":"Greek has one word for the whole temple complex with its courts and another, used here, for the building itself where God was held to dwell. Most English versions use “temple” for both words, though the NRSV also has “sanctuary” in this passage."},{"verse":15,"phrase":"beer","lemma":"σίκερα","kind":"departure","traditional":"strong drink","note":"The Greek word is borrowed from Hebrew and covers intoxicating drinks not made from grapes, most commonly beer brewed from grain. “Strong drink” now suggests distilled spirits, which were unknown in the ancient world. Some versions have “other fermented drink”, and the exact range of the term is uncertain."},{"verse":28,"phrase":"favored one","lemma":"χαριτόω","kind":"departure","traditional":"full of grace; highly favored","note":"The Greek is a single participle meaning one who has been shown favor, and it is taken up in verse 30, “you have found favor with God”. “Full of grace” comes from the Latin Bible and can suggest a quality Mary possesses, where the Greek describes something done for her. The word for “Greetings” is the ordinary Greek salutation, though some hear in it its literal sense, “rejoice”."},{"verse":28,"phrase":"The Lord is with you","lemma":"","kind":"textual","traditional":"The Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women (KJV)","note":"Many later manuscripts add “Blessed are you among women” at the end of the greeting. The earliest witnesses lack the words, and they are generally thought to have been copied in from Elizabeth’s greeting in verse 42."},{"verse":34,"phrase":"since I have never been with a man","lemma":"γινώσκω","kind":"departure","traditional":"seeing I know not a man; since I am a virgin","note":"Literally “since I do not know a man”, using the biblical idiom in which “know” refers to sexual relations. The literal form can be misheard today as a statement about acquaintance, so the idiom is translated by its meaning."},{"verse":35,"phrase":"the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God","lemma":"","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God (KJV)","note":"The Greek can also be read “the holy one to be born will be called Son of God”, taking “holy” with the one born instead of with “called”. Both readings are grammatical and both have scholarly support; the choice does not change the main claim of the verse."},{"verse":37,"phrase":"no word from God will fail","lemma":"ῥῆμα","kind":"departure","traditional":"nothing will be impossible with God","note":"The Greek says literally that “every word from God will not be powerless”, echoing the question put to Abraham about Sarah’s child in Genesis 18:14. The noun can mean “thing” as well as “word”, which gives the traditional rendering; that rendering also fits a slightly different text found in many manuscripts (“with God” for “from God”). “Word” is kept here because Mary takes it up at once in verse 38, “according to your word”."},{"verse":38,"phrase":"slave","lemma":"δούλη","kind":"departure","traditional":"handmaid; servant","note":"The Greek is the ordinary feminine word for a slave, someone who belongs to a master, not a hired servant. In the Septuagint it is also how a woman speaks of herself before God or a superior, as Hannah does in 1 Samuel 1:11, so it expresses belonging and readiness more than degradation. Most versions soften it to “servant”; “handmaid” is the older form."},{"verse":46,"phrase":"proclaims the greatness of","lemma":"μεγαλύνω","kind":"departure","traditional":"magnifies","note":"The verb means to make great and, with God as its object, to declare great or extol. “Magnifies” is the traditional rendering, from which the song gets its Latin name, the Magnificat, but in current English the word suggests enlarging an image. The same verb returns in verse 58, where the Lord “had shown the greatness of his mercy”."},{"verse":78,"phrase":"the dawn from on high","lemma":"ἀνατολή","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"the dayspring from on high; the sunrise","note":"The word means a rising, usually of the sun or a star, and the next line about light for those in darkness supports “dawn”. In the Septuagint the same word also translates the Hebrew for the “Branch”, a title of the coming Davidic king (Jeremiah 23:5; Zechariah 3:8; 6:12), and many scholars think both images are in view."},{"verse":78,"phrase":"will visit","lemma":"ἐπισκέπτομαι","kind":"textual","traditional":"hath visited (KJV)","note":"Many manuscripts read the past tense, “has visited”, matching verse 68. The future is found in the earliest witnesses and is the reading translated here; the past tense is usually explained as an adjustment to the earlier verse."}],"candidates":[{"lemma":"δούλη","rendering":"slave","verse":38,"reason":"The δοῦλος family recurs throughout the New Testament and versions split between “slave”, “servant” and “handmaid”, so Mary’s self-description needs to match the decision made for δοῦλος elsewhere."},{"lemma":"εὐλογέω","rendering":"bless / blessed","verse":42,"reason":"εὐλογημένος and εὐλογητός collide in English with μακάριος, which the register also renders “blessed”, and a single policy is needed on whether and how to keep them apart."},{"lemma":"ἰδού","rendering":"look","verse":20,"reason":"The particle occurs some two hundred times and versions vary between “behold”, “look”, “see”, “listen” and omission, so readers would see arbitrary variation without one rule."},{"lemma":"παῖς","rendering":"servant","verse":54,"reason":"The word can mean servant or child and is applied to Israel, David and Jesus (Acts 3–4), so its rendering and its distinction from δοῦλος should be fixed once."},{"lemma":"ἀγαλλίασις","rendering":"delight","verse":14,"reason":"The noun and its verb ἀγαλλιάω recur across Luke–Acts, John, 1 Peter and elsewhere beside χαρά and χαίρω, and need a consistent rendering distinct from “joy” and “rejoice”."}]}

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Since many have undertaken to compile an account of the things that have been fulfilled among us,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: just as they were handed down to us by those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: it seemed good to me also, having followed everything carefully from the start, to write it out for you in order, most excellent Theophilus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah. His wife was from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Both of them were righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and righteous requirements of the Lord.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were well advanced in their days.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now while Zechariah was serving as priest before God, when his division was on duty,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to enter the sanctuary of the Lord and burn incense.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of the incense offering.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the angel said to him,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to name him John.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: You will have joy and delight, and many will rejoice at his birth,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: for he will be great before the Lord. He must never drink wine or beer, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: He will turn many of the children of Israel back to the Lord their God.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: He himself will go on before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to make ready for the Lord a people prepared.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Zechariah said to the angel,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “How will I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is well advanced in her days.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The angel answered him,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “I am Gabriel, who stands before God, and I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: And look, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Meanwhile the people were waiting for Zechariah, and they were amazed that he was taking so long in the sanctuary.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he came out he could not speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the sanctuary. He kept making signs to them and remained mute.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When his days of service were completed, he went back to his home.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After those days his wife Elizabeth conceived, and she kept herself hidden for five months, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This is what the Lord has done for me in the days when he looked on me, to take away my disgrace among people.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a town in Galilee named Nazareth,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of the house of David. The virgin’s name was Mary.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He came to her and said,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Greetings, favored one! The Lord is with you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But she was deeply troubled at his words and pondered what kind of greeting this might be.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The angel said to her,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: Look, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: He will be great and will be called Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: He will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mary said to the angel,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “How will this be, since I have never been with a man?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The angel answered her,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: And look, your relative Elizabeth has also conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: For no word from God will fail.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mary said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, I am the Lord’s slave. May it happen to me according to your word.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the angel left her.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In those days Mary set out and went in haste to the hill country, to a town of Judah.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She cried out with a loud voice and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For look, when the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby in my womb leaped with delight.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And blessed is she who believed that what was spoken to her from the Lord would be accomplished.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Mary said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “My soul proclaims the greatness of the Lord,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and my spirit delights in God my Savior,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: for he has looked on the lowliness of his slave. For look, from now on all generations will call me blessed,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: for the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: His mercy is for those who fear him, from generation to generation.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered those who are proud in the thoughts of their hearts.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: He has brought down rulers from thrones and lifted up the lowly;

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: the hungry he has filled with good things, and the rich he has sent away empty.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: He has come to the aid of Israel his servant, remembering mercy,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: just as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his offspring forever.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mary stayed with her about three months and then returned to her home.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown the greatness of his mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were going to call him Zechariah, after his father.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But his mother spoke up and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “No! He will be called John.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to her,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “There is no one among your relatives who is called by that name.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they made signs to his father to ask what he wanted him to be called.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He asked for a writing tablet and wrote,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “John is his name.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they were all amazed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At once his mouth was opened and his tongue set free, and he began to speak, blessing God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Fear came on all who lived around them, and all these things were talked about throughout the hill country of Judea.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: All who heard them stored them up in their hearts, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What then will this child be?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For indeed the hand of the Lord was with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, for he has visited his people and worked redemption for them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: just as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: to show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: the oath that he swore to Abraham our father, to grant us

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: that we, rescued from the hand of enemies, might serve him without fear

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: in holiness and righteousness before him all our days.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And you, child, will be called prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: to give his people knowledge of salvation in the forgiveness of their sins,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: through the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: to shine on those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The child grew and became strong in spirit, and he was in the wilderness until the day of his public appearance to Israel.

notes.note: The verb can mean to bring something to completion or to convince someone fully. The KJV took it the second way; most modern scholars and versions take it the first way, of events that have run their full course, probably with the overtone that God’s promises were carried out in them.

The verb is the ordinary one for passing teaching or testimony from one generation to the next. Older versions have “delivered”, which no longer conveys that sense; several modern versions already use “handed down” or “handed on”.

The verb can mean formal instruction or simply being told a report, as it does in Acts 21:21. On the first reading Theophilus is a believer who has received Christian teaching; on the second he may be an interested outsider who has heard about these events. Most scholars favor instruction, but the question remains open.

The priests were organized into twenty-four divisions, each named for an ancestral head; Abijah’s is the eighth in the list in 1 Chronicles 24. The divisions took turns serving at the temple for a week at a time, so an ordinary priest spent most of the year at home.

The Greek word belongs to the same family as “righteous” earlier in the verse, a link the usual renderings hide. Greek has one word-family where English has two (righteous and just, righteousness and justice), so the same root can surface in English under either. The meaning here, the specific things God requires, is not disputed.

Greek has one word for the whole temple complex with its courts and another, used here, for the building itself where God was held to dwell. Only priests entered that building, which is why the people wait outside in verse 10. Most English versions use “temple” for both words, though the NRSV also has “sanctuary” in this passage.

The Greek word is borrowed from Hebrew and covers intoxicating drinks not made from grapes, most commonly beer brewed from grain. “Strong drink” now suggests distilled spirits, which were unknown in the ancient world. Some versions have “other fermented drink”, and the exact range of the term is uncertain.

The Greek is a single participle meaning one who has been shown favor, and it is taken up in verse 30, “you have found favor with God”. “Full of grace” comes from the Latin Bible and can suggest a quality Mary possesses, where the Greek describes something done for her. The word for “Greetings” is the ordinary Greek salutation, though some hear in it its literal sense, “rejoice”.

notes.traditional: The Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women (KJV)
notes.note: Many later manuscripts add “Blessed are you among women” at the end of the greeting. The earliest witnesses lack the words, and they are generally thought to have been copied in from Elizabeth’s greeting in verse 42.

notes.phrase: since I have never been with a man
notes.traditional: seeing I know not a man; since I am a virgin
notes.note: Literally “since I do not know a man”, using the biblical idiom in which “know” refers to sexual relations. The literal form can be misheard today as a statement about acquaintance, so the idiom is translated by its meaning.

notes.phrase: the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God
notes.traditional: that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God (KJV)
notes.note: The Greek can also be read “the holy one to be born will be called Son of God”, taking “holy” with the one born instead of with “called”. Both readings are grammatical and both have scholarly support; the choice does not change the main claim of the verse.

notes.phrase: no word from God will fail
notes.traditional: nothing will be impossible with God
notes.note: The Greek says literally that “every word from God will not be powerless”, echoing the question put to Abraham about Sarah’s child in Genesis 18:14. The noun can mean “thing” as well as “word”, which gives the traditional rendering; that rendering also fits a slightly different text found in many manuscripts (“with God” for “from God”). “Word” is kept here because Mary takes it up at once in verse 38, “according to your word”.

The Greek is the ordinary feminine word for a slave, someone who belongs to a master, not a hired servant. In the Septuagint it is also how a woman speaks of herself before God or a superior, as Hannah does in 1 Samuel 1:11, so it expresses belonging and readiness more than degradation. Most versions soften it to “servant”; “handmaid” is the older form.

The verb means to make great and, with God as its object, to declare great or extol. “Magnifies” is the traditional rendering, from which the song gets its Latin name, the Magnificat, but in current English the word suggests enlarging an image. The same verb returns in verse 58, where the Lord “had shown the greatness of his mercy”.

notes.traditional: the dayspring from on high; the sunrise
notes.note: The word means a rising, usually of the sun or a star, and the next line about light for those in darkness supports “dawn”. In the Septuagint the same word also translates the Hebrew for the “Branch”, a title of the coming Davidic king (Jeremiah 23:5; Zechariah 3:8; 6:12), and many scholars think both images are in view.

Many manuscripts read the past tense, “has visited”, matching verse 68. The future is found in the earliest witnesses and is the reading translated here; the past tense is usually explained as an adjustment to the earlier verse.

candidates.reason: The δοῦλος family recurs throughout the New Testament and versions split between “slave”, “servant” and “handmaid”, so Mary’s self-description needs to match the decision made for δοῦλος elsewhere.
εὐλογημένος and εὐλογητός collide in English with μακάριος, which the register also renders “blessed”, and a single policy is needed on whether and how to keep them apart.
The particle occurs some two hundred times and versions vary between “behold”, “look”, “see”, “listen” and omission, so readers would see arbitrary variation without one rule.
The word can mean servant or child and is applied to Israel, David and Jesus (Acts 3–4), so its rendering and its distinction from δοῦλος should be fixed once.
The noun and its verb ἀγαλλιάω recur across Luke–Acts, John, 1 Peter and elsewhere beside χαρά and χαίρω, and need a consistent rendering distinct from “joy” and “rejoice”.
